'''Arthur James Guyton''' (born February 12, 1978) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and now basketball coach. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]].

== Indiana University ==
Guyton chose to play basketball at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] under coach [[Bob Knight]] during 1996. His 283 [[three-pointers]] were the most for Indiana when his playing career ended in 2000. Guyton also had 2,100 points with the team.<ref name="Houser">{{cite news|last=Houser|first=Lynn|title=Guyton: Indiana's forgotten star|url=http://www.heraldtimesonline.com/hoosiershq/historia/cuw/?sid=173|access-date=9 April 2012|newspaper=Herald-Times|date=15 January 2007}}</ref>  In 2000, he was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Co-MVP and that same year was selected to the first team [[2000 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2000 All-American Team]]. His senior year was a successful one in which he averaged 19.7 points per game.{{citation needed|date=February 2025}}

Guyton later recalled, "I remember it all like it was yesterday. Those are nights you live for. I felt back then I couldn't be guarded."<ref name="Houser"/> On June 10, 2014, Guyton learned that he was being inducted into the Indiana University Basketball Hall of Fame.{{citation needed|date=February 2025}}

== Professional career ==
Guyton was selected by the [[Chicago Bulls]] in the second round (32nd overall pick) in the [[2000 NBA draft]]. He played for the Bulls from 2000 to 2002 and briefly for the [[Golden State Warriors]] during the [[2002–03 NBA season|2002–03 season]]. During his career in the NBA, he played in 80 games and averaged 5.5 points, 1 rebound and 1.8 assists. His final NBA game was played on November 20, 2002, in a 100–94 win over the Chicago Bulls where he only played for 30 seconds and recorded no stats. He later played in the [[NBDL]], [[Italy]], [[Israel]], [[Croatia]], and [[Sweden]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=SWE&PlayerID=24858&AmNotSure=1 A.J. Guyton] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081009200158/http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=SWE&PlayerID=24858&AmNotSure=1 |date=October 9, 2008 }}. Eurobasket.com</ref>

== Post-player career ==
In 2010 Guyton was an assistant coach at [[Illinois Central College]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.icc.edu/athletics/basketballM/coachingStaff.asp |title=ICC Athletics - Men's Basketball :: Coaching Staff |access-date=2011-02-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101216160756/http://icc.edu/athletics/basketballM/coachingStaff.asp |archive-date=2010-12-16 }}</ref> He was also head coach of the [[Bloomington Flex]], a minor league team located in the Bloomington, Illinois area.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.pantagraph.com/sports/basketball/professional/article_65fefc90-ead7-11e0-8cfc-001cc4c002e0.html |title=Central Illinois Drive name of B-N hoops team |access-date=November 27, 2011 |archive-date=March 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320175349/https://pantagraph.com/sports/basketball/professional/article_65fefc90-ead7-11e0-8cfc-001cc4c002e0.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Guyton led the Flex, then known as the Central Illinois Drive, to a 22–1 record in 2012 and a Premier Basketball League championship.  Guyton also led the Flex to a PBL title in 2013, winning Coach of the Year honors both seasons.  In 2014, the Flex were again the top team in the PBL under Guyton's leadership, finishing the season with a perfect 18–0 record.

In 2015, Guyton was appointed Consulting Director with the [[Midwest Professional Basketball Association]].<ref name="MPBA-front-office">{{cite web |url=http://www.thempba.com/page/show/1468507-front-office |title=Front Office |work=MPBA web site |access-date=2014-11-21 |quote=A.J. Guyton, Consulting Director |archive-date=November 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141125233948/http://www.thempba.com/page/show/1468507-front-office |url-status=live }}</ref>

On September 30, 2016, Guyton was appointed an assistant coach of the [[Windy City Bulls]], a new [[NBA Development League]] franchise.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-finalize-coaching-basketball-operations-staff-inaugural-season/|title=Windy City Bulls Finalize Coaching & Basketball Operations Staff For Inaugural Season|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=September 30, 2016|access-date=October 1, 2016|archive-date=October 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161009150710/http://windycity.dleague.nba.com/news/windy-city-bulls-finalize-coaching-basketball-operations-staff-inaugural-season/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2017, Guyton was named the director of player development for the [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nusports.com/coaches.aspx?rc=1418&path=mbball |title=NU Sports - 2017-18 Men's Basketball Coaching Staff |access-date=2018-04-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180419120453/https://nusports.com/coaches.aspx?rc=1418&path=mbball |archive-date=2018-04-19 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In June 2018, Guyton was named an assistant coach for the [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball]] team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/2018/06/20/former-iu-basketball-player-j-guyton-joins-loyola-university-maryland-coaching-staff/717739002/|title=Former IU basketball player A.J. Guyton joins Loyola-Maryland coaching staff}}</ref>
